title: 2026 Massachusetts Gubernatorial Election
description: The 2026 Massachusetts gubernatorial election is scheduled for November 3, 2026, with the primary on September 1, 2026. Incumbent Democratic Governor Maura Healey is seeking a second term, having assumed office in January 2023 after defeating Republican nominee Geoff Diehl in the 2022 general election. Massachusetts has no gubernatorial term limits. The Republican field narrowed to two candidates—former Abiomed CEO Mike Minogue and former MBTA chief administrator Brian Shortsleeve—after the April 2026 state GOP convention, where Minogue won the party endorsement with over 70% of delegate votes. This race is being closely watched as a test of Democratic strength in a reliably blue state, with early polling showing Healey holding double-digit leads over both potential Republican opponents.

candidates.name: Maura Healey
candidates.summary: Maura Healey is the 73rd Governor of Massachusetts, first elected in 2022 and serving since January 2023. She previously served as Massachusetts Attorney General from 2015 to 2023. Healey is the first woman and first openly lesbian person elected governor of Massachusetts. She is running for re-election on a platform focused on lowering costs, expanding affordable housing, and protecting access to health care and reproductive rights.

candidates.name: Mike Minogue
candidates.summary: Mike Minogue is a former CEO of Abiomed, a Danvers-based medical device company, and a retired U.S. Army infantry officer who served in Operation Desert Storm. He graduated from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1989 with a degree in engineering. Minogue won the Massachusetts Republican Party's endorsement at the April 2026 state convention with over 70% of delegate votes, positioning him as the frontrunner for the Republican nomination. His campaign focuses on cutting taxes, auditing state government, addressing illegal immigration, and reducing the cost of living.

candidates.name: Brian Shortsleeve
candidates.summary: Brian Shortsleeve is a former Chief Administrator and Acting General Manager of the MBTA, a Marine Corps veteran who served in Bosnia and the Persian Gulf, and co-founder of M33 Growth, a venture capital firm. He graduated from Harvard College on an ROTC scholarship and earned an MBA from Harvard Business School. Shortsleeve narrowly cleared the 15% threshold at the April 2026 Massachusetts Republican convention to qualify for the September primary ballot. His campaign emphasizes cutting waste in government, reducing taxes, auditing state agencies, and restoring fiscal responsibility.

forecast.rationale: Available general-election polling consistently shows incumbent Democrat Maura Healey leading both Republican contenders by double digits to high double digits in a strongly Democratic state. Across four Healey-vs-Republican matchup polls from April to May, Healey leads Mike Minogue by 20 and 27 points and Brian Shortsleeve by 22 and 29 points. Healey also benefits from incumbency and Massachusetts' recent Democratic lean. Confidence is reduced somewhat because the general-election polling is limited in quantity, the Republican nominee is not yet finalized, and the race is still months from the primary and general election.
